name: Bakung Kenyah
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: Only Glottolog ref is an ISO 639-3 merge request (boc merged into Mainstream Kenyah xkl); no descriptive work specific to Bakung found.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (rev. ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics. Sec. 4.1.3.
sources.note: Areal remark only: many coastal Sarawak and some interior Borneo languages have final stress in citation forms but penultimate stress in phrasal context; Lowland Kenyah of Long San etc. 'have final stress in citation forms'; 'Highland Kenyah' named only for syllabification of geminates. No Bakung/Usun Apau statement.

sources.citation: Yan, Meri Tiana, Praptomo Baryadi Isodarus & Maria Magdalena Sinta Wardani. 2019. Imbuhan pembentuk kata kerja dalam bahasa Dayak Kenyah Bakung. Sintesis 13(2): 82-92.
sources.note: Nothing; Bakung-specific but verbal affixation only (morphophonemic nasal substitution noted, no prosody).

sources.citation: Asih, Yuni Utami. 2017. Inventory of Kenyah Lepo Tau segmental sounds. OKARA: Jurnal Bahasa dan Sastra 11(1): 1-10. DOI 10.19105/ojbs.v11i1.1233.
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Segmental inventory of Kenyah Lepo' Tau (same ISO language [xkl]) compared with 'LB' = Lepo' Bakung after Rufinus 1992 'Lepo' Bakung Sound System' (Borneo Research Council, 15 pp.), Lees 1965 and Soriente 2003; mentions consonant gemination and vowel length after penultimate schwa only.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2017. The Lowland Kenyah posterior implosives. Language and Linguistics 18(2): 177-200. DOI 10.1075/lali.18.2.01blu.
sources.note: Appendix fn. 11, p.198: 'Stress was invariably recorded as final in citation forms.' -- for Long San/Long Sela'an/Long Ikang (Lebu' Vu', Western Lowland Kenyah = long1406), a different Kenyah language; nothing on Bakung or Highland/Usun Apau Kenyah.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: No Bakung data (Kenyah varieties: Lepo' Tau, Lepo' Sawa, Lepo' Gah, Lepo' Laang, Badeng, Lebo' Vo', Uma' Pawe, Penan, Sebop) and no statement on Kenyah stress; stress remarks concern Merap, Murik, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh only.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2008. The classification of Kenyah languages: a preliminary statement. SEALS XIV vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics E-5), 49-62; and Soriente, Antonia (ed.) 2006. Mencaleny & Usung Bayung Marang, front matter (orthography notes).
sources.note: Nothing on accent placement in any Kenyah variety (a full-text search for stress/accent-confirmed).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request Number 2007-245 (submitted by Karl Anderbeck, SIL Indonesia): rename [xkl] 'Mainstream Kenyah'; merge Madang [mqd] and Kenyah, Bakung [boc] into [xkl], following Soriente (2005). 9 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; identity/classification only (Bakung = Soriente's Usun Apau/Mainstream Kenyah 'Group 4' with Lepo Teppu').

sources.citation: Eghenter, Cristina, Bernard Sellato & G. Simon Devung (eds.). 2003. Social Science Research and Conservation Management in the Interior of Borneo. Bogor: CIFOR/WWF Indonesia/UNESCO/Ford Foundation. Incl. ch. 12: C. Yus Ngabut, 'Kenyah Bakung oral literature: an introduction', pp. 241-257, and consolidated bibliography (pp. 275ff).
sources.note: Nothing. Ngabut gives Bakung (Long Apan Baru/Long Aran, Pujungan) interlinear text samples and states (p.243) that the transcriptions were used by 'language specialists, in their studies of Bakung phonology, morphology, and syntax' (Sri Munawarah 1995; Morgan et al. 1996); bibliography names the unpublished Bakung reports Rufinus 1995, Sri Munawarah 1995 (34 pp.), Hanye 1995, Morgan et al. 1996 dictionary, Soriente 1999, Soriente 2002 PhD.

sources.citation: Guerreiro, Antonio J. 1996. Homophony, sound changes and dialectal variations in some central Bornean languages. Mon-Khmer Studies 25: 205-226.
sources.note: Nothing on Kenyah stress; Kayanic (Kayan/Modang/Bahau) sound changes, Kenyah cited only for loans/wordlists (Soriente 1994). Image-only PDF, scanned (tesseract, 300 dpi).

sources.citation: The Sarawak Museum Journal vol. 1 (1911-1913), archive.org scanned text, containing Douglas, R.S. 1911 'A comparative vocabulary of the Kayan, Kenyah and Kalabit dialects' and Ray, Sidney H. 1913 'The languages of Borneo' SMJ 1(4): 1-196.
sources.note: Nothing for Kenyah (vocabularies and classification; the only stress remark in the volume concerns Ngaju/Mantangai sentence-final stress).

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul & Alexander D. Smith. 2024. Non-Malayic languages of Borneo. In K. Alexander Adelaar & Antoinette Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, ch. 27. Oxford: OUP.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Modern authoritative survey with an explicit Kenyah stress passage (from Blust's fieldnotes: penultimate stress, final after penultimate schwa) seen only in snippets; need the full text to identify the variety and any Highland/Usun Apau Kenyah statement.
sources.venue: The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, ch

sources.citation: Sri Munawarah. 1995 [1994]. Struktur Kebahasaan Kenyah (Leppo') Bakung di Desa Long Apan Baru. Unpublished report, Culture & Conservation, Kayan Mentarang Conservation Project, WWF Indonesia Programme & Ditjen PHPA, Jakarta. 34 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Structural sketch of Bakung (phonology, morphology, syntax per Ngabut 2003:243); likely has a 'tekanan' paragraph; held in WWF-Indonesia/CIFOR C&C report series.
sources.venue: Struktur Kebahasaan Kenyah (Leppo') Bakung di Desa Long Apan Baru

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2004 [thesis 2003]. A Classification of Kenyah Variants in Sarawak and Kalimantan. PhD thesis, Fakulti Sains Sosial dan Kemanusiaan, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia, Bangi. xvii+400 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Contains phonological descriptions of each Kenyah variant (Lepo' Tau phonology pp. 77-80 cited by Asih 2017) including Group-4 Bakung; would give a first-hand stress statement for Bakung and for [xkl] generally.
sources.venue: A Classification of Kenyah Variants in Sarawak and Kalimantan

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 1997. The Kenyah isolects of Long Pujungan District in North-East Kalimantan. In Cecilia Odé & Wim Stokhof (eds.), Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics, 713-738. Amsterdam/Atlanta: Rodopi.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: First-hand dialectological/phonological survey of the Pujungan Kenyah isolects including Bakung of Long Aran; most likely published locus of a Bakung prosody remark.
sources.venue: Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics

sources.citation: Rufinus, Albert. 1992. Lepo' Bakung Sound System. Paper presented to the Borneo Research Council (Second Biennial International Conference, Kota Kinabalu), 15 pp. [cited as 'Malaysia: Borneo Research Council, 1992, pp. 1-15' by Asih 2017; reported in Borneo Research Bulletin 26 (1995) as 'Kenyah Bakung sound system']; cf. Rufinus, A. 1995. Sistem Kebahasaan Lepo' Bakung di Apan Baru, Long Pujungan. C&C report, WWF/PHPA Jakarta.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Kenyah Bakung (Long Apan Baru); a sound-system paper of this kind normally states stress placement.

sources.citation: Lees, Shirley P. 1965. An introduction to the sound system of Lépu' Tau. Sarawak Museum Journal 12 (25-26, n.s.): 179-184.
